sources.title: Moving the self and others to do good: The emotional underpinnings of prosocial behavior
Why Awe Promotes Prosocial Behaviors? The Mediating Effects of Future Time Perspective and Self-Transcendence Meaning of Life
sources.authors: Li JJ, Dou K, Wang YJ, Nie YG.

findings.finding: Awe arises when we encounter stimuli that exceed our existing mental structures, requiring us to adjust our perspective.
findings.quote: the emotion of awe (i.e., challenge that exceeds the scope of one's mental structures, requiring cognitive accommodation) awakens self-transcendence

findings.finding: Experiencing awe can help learners feel less focused on their individual concerns and more connected to the world around them.
findings.quote: When describing the experience of natural beauty, participants were more likely to report that they felt unaware of day-to-day concerns, felt the presence of something greater

findings.finding: Awe is linked to improved well-being and a greater sense of meaning, which can foster a more positive learning environment.
findings.quote: Awe involves five processes linked to well-being: "shifts in neurophysiology, a diminished focus on the self, increased prosocial relationality, greater social integration, and a heightened sense of meaning."

principle: Awe is an emotion triggered by vast or complex experiences that challenge our current understanding, leading to a diminished focus on the self and an increased sense of connection to others.
for_the_teacher: Incorporate music or visual elements that evoke a sense of vastness or beauty to help students shift their focus away from day-to-day anxieties.
Encourage students to reflect on the 'bigger picture' of their movement practice to foster a sense of self-transcendence and connection to the dance community.
when_it_does_not_apply: Awe may not be experienced if the stimulus is easily assimilated into existing knowledge or if the individual is in actual physical danger.
